capabilities.label: Verified local account registration

entities.name: pending-registration
entities.identity: opaque pending id bound to one browser session

entities.name: local-account
entities.identity: site-local account id and unique normalized email

transitions.trigger: correct unexpired code within attempt budget
transactional account creation and session rotation

server_authorities: The server normalizes identity and hashes password and code.
An account is created only after successful verification.
Duplicate normalized email creation is rejected transactionally.

not_applicable.rationale: The pending verification challenge is single-use with a server-side wall-clock expiry in the vendored auth store; the gate runs under a frozen clock that is never advanced, so the expired-challenge branch is not exercised here.
Registration mints a new session-bound account and owns no pre-existing owner-scoped resource, so there is no cross-account authorization boundary to cross.
Registration is a public pre-authentication action with no role precondition to enforce.

This capability's account, session, verification-challenge, and mail-outbox tables are provisioned and versioned by the vendored websitebench.site_backend runtime (create_account_subject is invoked by that store inside its own registration transaction), not by the site business migration ledger; site business-table migration linearity is proven separately by test_migration_ledger_is_linear_and_complete.

Every write for this capability executes through the shared single-writer connection path (connect() opens WAL with BEGIN IMMEDIATE and busy_timeout=5000, serializing writers); that serialization is exercised under real concurrent threads by test_concurrent_duplicate_add_converges_to_one_row, but this capability's own write path is not separately contended here.

capabilities.label: Enumeration-resistant local password recovery

entities.name: password-reset-challenge
entities.identity: opaque reset id bound to one browser session

transitions.trigger: correct unexpired code within attempt budget
password is replaced and sessions are revoked

server_authorities: Known and unknown emails receive indistinguishable public responses.
Only the server binds a reset flow to an account.
Password replacement revokes prior authenticated sessions.

not_applicable.rationale: Each reset request supersedes any prior session-bound challenge rather than accumulating duplicates.
The reset-code challenge carries a wall-clock TTL in the vendored auth store; the frozen gate clock is never advanced, so the expired-challenge branch is not exercised here.
The flow is session-bound and, by its enumeration-safe design, never reveals or targets another owner's account.
Password recovery is a public pre-authentication action with no role precondition.

A reset challenge is ephemeral session-bound state; no in-flight challenge is replayed across a cold restart in these tests, and the durable account it targets is covered by the shared restart-persistence database proof.

capabilities.label: Truthful local verification and recovery mail outbox

entities.name: mail-outbox-entry
entities.identity: site-local outbox id and purpose-bound flow id

transitions.trigger: operator enables complete explicit SMTP configuration
delivery attempt fails or ceiling is reached
bounded idempotent retry below the delivery ceiling

server_authorities: Offline mode records LOCAL_ONLY and never claims external delivery.
SMTP is disabled unless every required setting is present.
Claim, retry, and startup replay share one delivery ceiling.

not_applicable.rationale: The outbox records exactly what the server enqueues; malformed user input is rejected by the triggering capability before any mail is enqueued, so there is no invalid-mail path at this layer.
Each enqueue is a distinct purpose-bound outbox entry; idempotency lives on the triggering account or challenge, not on the mail record.
Offline mail is recorded LOCAL_ONLY with no SMTP transition; the delivery-ceiling and retry states are unreachable under the frozen offline configuration.
Outbox entries are system-scoped operational records, not owner-scoped resources, so there is no cross-owner boundary.
Enqueueing mail is an internal server effect with no client-facing role gate.
Outbox rows live in the vendored mail store; no outbox entry is read back across a cold restart in these tests.

This capability's account, session, verification-challenge, and mail-outbox tables are provisioned and versioned by the vendored websitebench.site_backend runtime (create_account_subject is invoked by that store inside its own registration transaction), not by the site business migration ledger; site business-table migration linearity is proven separately by test_migration_ledger_is_linear_and_complete.

capabilities.label: Owner-scoped trip itinerary plan management

entities.name: trip
entities.identity: site-local trip id owned by exactly one account

entities.name: itinerary-plan
entities.identity: site-local plan id within an owned trip or the Unfiled bucket

entities.name: write-command
entities.identity: per-owner idempotency-key ledger entry and plan natural key

transitions.trigger: owner submits a valid plan to an owned trip or Unfiled
idempotent re-submit by command key or natural key is absorbed without a new row
owner reassigns the plan to another owned trip or to Unfiled

server_authorities: Ownership is resolved from the server session; foreign or missing trips read and mutate as 404 without disclosing existence.
The server validates plan fields (for example check-out on or after check-in) and rejects illegal input before any write.
Writes are idempotent by command key and by natural key, so re-submits and concurrent duplicates converge to a single row.
Timeline order is computed by the server from start timestamp then sort key, independent of insertion order.

not_applicable.rationale: Itinerary mutations are last-writer-wins over durable rows with no expiring challenge or optimistic-version token; safe form re-submission is instead covered by the command-ledger idempotency under the duplicate obligation.
